expected: VAS recognises rent expense on a straight-line basis. IFRS recognises a right-of-use asset and lease liability at commencement.
raw:
VAS: A lessee must recognize a right-of-use asset and lease liability at commencement. Straight-line expense is typically used unless another method is more suitable. [VAS 06]
IFRS: At commencement, a lessee recognizes a right-of-use asset and lease liability if the lease term exceeds twelve months. For low-value leases, relief may be applied. [IFRS 16]
COMPARE: Both standards require recognition of an asset and liability upon commencement but differ on how long-term leases are treated. VAS allows straight-line expense regardless of lease duration, while IFRS provides relief for low-value leases.
final:
**VAS** — A lessee must recognize a right-of-use asset and lease liability at commencement. Straight-line expense is typically used unless another method is more suitable. [C1]

**IFRS** — At commencement, a lessee recognizes a right-of-use asset and lease liability if the lease term exceeds twelve months. For low-value leases, relief may be applied. [C2]
